label: CONTAINED_IN_2, intentional: in the bearer and apprehended as a content about a candidate
definition: ContainsIntentionally Contains About Apprehends b e: the item e is contained in the bearer b, it is about some candidate, and b itself apprehends it. It is the reading of 'the form of another in the knower as of another': the bearer has the candidate present as object. Examples: an architect's idea of a house; on the personal account, a divine idea. Non-examples: a power of b to produce x that b does not apprehend; a mode in which b's nature is imitable by x, not apprehended. Reduced to the free relations Contains, About and Apprehends; the classical difference between having the form of another as other and having the power to produce it is captured only through Apprehends.
